cli.usage.label: Usage:
cli.usage.section.paths: CLI Paths (commands with a cli_path; local when the folder has a kai.yml):
cli.usage.paths_discover: kai [path...]                 lists the available paths (the root, or inside a folder)
cli.usage.paths_run: kai <path...> <args>          runs the command (required args positional, optional --name=value)
cli.usage.paths_global: kai -g <path...>              uses the app's global paths even with a local file (or --global)
cli.usage.paths_detached: kai -d <path...> <args>       runs in the background and hands the terminal back (combine: -gd)
cli.usage.paths_window: kai -gw <path...> <args>      also opens the output in its own window (or --window; needs -g)
cli.usage.run: kai run <command-name>        runs a command by name
cli.usage.env_use: kai env use <name>            activates an environment
cli.usage.import: kai import [file|folder]      imports a project kai.yml or an exported package (--only a,b picks parts)
cli.import.unsupported_file: '%1' isn't a project file — use kai.yml.
cli.import.only_needs_package: --only only applies to an exported package (a file with the kai_export header).
cli.import.unknown_only: Unknown --only name '%1'. Use: commands, collections, settings, environments, terminal-profiles, actions, global-actions, action-commands.
cli.raise.no_tray: No system tray in this environment: the notification was only added to Kai's history.
cli.usage.raise: kai raise [--level <level>] <msg>  notification in Kai's tray (info, warning, error)
cli.usage.validate: kai validate <file>           checks a kai.yml for structural errors
cli.usage.completion: kai completion <bash|zsh|powershell>   prints the Tab autocomplete script for your shell
cli.error.usage.completion: Usage: kai completion <bash|zsh|powershell|pwsh> | kai completion install|uninstall [bash|zsh|powershell|pwsh]

kip.cli.help:
kai kip — helper for programs that speak KIP (Kai Interface Protocol).
Prints ONE protocol message per call on stdout. Pure and offline: no Kai app needed.

Usage: kai kip <verb> [options]

Verbs:
  hello    [--title T] [--version V]
  prompt   --id ID [--title T] [--description D] [--submit-label L] [--back] [--no-cancel] [--no-remember]
           --field <type> <name> [label] [field options]   (repeat --field for more fields)
  confirm  --id ID --text TEXT [--title T] [--danger] [--confirm-label L] [--cancel-label L] [--back] [--no-cancel]
  patch    --id ID [--seq N] [--field ...] [--remove name[,name]] [--chip ... | --no-chips]
           (no --seq = a spontaneous patch, e.g. from a chip; with --seq it answers a `change`)
  chip-result <chip-id> <running|success|error> [text] [--title T] [--id PROMPT]
  invalid  --id ID [--error field=message]... [--message TEXT]
  message  [info|success|warning|error] TEXT
  markdown TEXT | --file PATH
  progress <0-100|null> [label] [--no-cancel]
  steps    --id ID [--title T] --item ID [label] [--state S] [--detail D] ...
  step     <steps-id> <item-id> <pending|running|success|error|skipped> [detail]
  table    [--id ID] [--title T] --column key:label ... --rows-json '[...]'
  notify   TITLE [TEXT] [--level L]
  set-env  NAME VALUE
  done     [--title T] [--text X] [--level L] [--action type:label:value]... [--path-format F]
  raw      '<json>'          validates a KIP message and prints it
  get      '<json>' <path>   prints a value from a response (e.g. values.env, values.opts.dry)

Field types: text secret textarea number date select list table filepick folderpick flags
Field options (apply to the LAST --field):
  --required  --default V  --placeholder T  --description T  --group G  --watch  --no-remember
  --options a,b,c  --option value:label[:description]  --multiple (list/table)
  --min N  --max N  --step N  --decimals N (number)   --mode date|time|datetime  --range (date)
  --flag name:label[:default] (flags)   --column key:label  --row-key K  --rows-json '[...]' (table)
  --filter '*.sql'  --initial-dir DIR  --path-format native|posix|windows (filepick/folderpick)
  --search  --no-search  --page-size N (list/table: filter box and pages of N items)
Chips (prompt/patch; the --chip-* options apply to the LAST --chip):
  --chip ID [label]  --chip-description T  --chip-icon NAME  --chip-danger  --chip-requires field[,field]
  --chip-confirm  --chip-confirm-title T  --chip-confirm-text T  --chip-confirm-label L  --chip-cancel-label L
Before the first --field, --description and --no-remember belong to the prompt itself.

Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 get: path not found · 2 invalid usage (message on stderr, nothing on stdout).

manifesto.title: Creation manifesto
manifesto.intro: Hand one of these guides to an AI assistant and it can write Kai files for you. Copy it, paste it at the start of the conversation, then describe what you want (for example "a kai.yml for this repository" or "a KIP wizard to deploy my app"). The text below is exactly what gets copied.
manifesto.kai.desc: How to write a project file in YAML: the YAML rules Kai's parser follows, the complete model of every structure (command, parameter, HTTP, collection, hooks, conditions, responders), complete example files, a checklist, and the list of valid icon names.
manifesto.kip.desc: How to write a program that talks KIP (forms, confirmations, progress, tables, chips) and register it in a kai.yml: the protocol, patterns, pitfalls, complete runnable examples in bash and Python, how to test it, and a checklist.
